Refugee Housing Units: Guide for NGOs, Governments, and Relief Organizations

2026-04-08

For people left homeless due to conflict or natural disasters, refugee housing units offer a reliable solution. Converted containers can be transformed into safe, insulated living units that also ensure privacy. These refugee camp containers are pre-insulated, pre-wired, stackable, deployed in 24 to 48 hours, and are durable, with a lifespan of over 20 years.

This guide details what a refugee housing unit is, technical specifications, key advantages, practical applications, and factors to consider—enabling you to make an informed purchasing decision.

What Is a Refugee Housing Unit?

Refugee housing unit is a modular, durable steel container housing unit designed for rapid deployment. They provide safe and insulated container accommodations as an alternative to traditional tents. These refugee container homes offer long-term, reusable housing solutions that can be configured to meet the needs of individual families, schools, or medical facilities, and are better equipped to withstand harsh weather.

Types of Modular Refugee Housing Configurations

  • • 20-foot Refugee Housing Units: Compact, portable — ideal for individual family units, medical triage stations, or command posts.
  • • 40-foot Refugee Housing Units: Larger footprint for dormitory use, storage, or expanded medical facilities.
  • • X-Type/Z-Type Foldable Refugee Housing Units: Factory-folded to a fraction of their deployed size; unfold into a complete structure within minutes on-site.
  • • Flat-pack Refugee Housing Units: Flat-pack container houses are shipped as individual panels and floor/roof components. On-site, the pre-welded roof and floor are assembled first, followed by the installation of wall panels and columns to form a sturdy structure.
  • • Detachable/Modular Refugee Housing Units: Modular container houses are shipped as a disassembled frame (columns, beams, panels) and bolted together on-site. These structures can be stacked up to three stories high or connected to form large-scale refugee camps or field hospitals.

NEW BRAND has manufactured and exported container housing units to 60+ countries [Company history to be supplied], offering all five configuration types with full customization, including climate-specific insulation, accessible layouts, and sanitation units. Please send an email to NEW BRAND@NEW BRAND.com for inquiries, and we will meet your needs.

Refugee Housing Units Design and Construction

Here's a modular refugee housing unit production, which is designed with comfort and durability in mind:

Structural Core

  • • Corten galvanized steel frame with anti-corrosion coating for temporary and long-duration units
  • • Class-A fire-rated wall, floor, and roof sandwich panels
  • • Pre-drilled bolt connections for rapid field assembly without welding

Insulation and Climate Control

  • • Climate-specific insulation options (EPS, rock wool, PU foam) for arctic, tropical, and arid environments
  • • Double-pane windows can improve insulation and reduce noise
  • • Pre-installed HVAC knock-outs for field-installed heating and cooling
  • • Reflective roof coatings to reduce solar heat gain in tropical climates

Utilities and Systems

  • • Pre-wired electrical conduit and distribution panel (solar-ready or grid-tied)
  • • Plumbing rough-in for water supply and wastewater connection
  • • Optional integrated sanitation blocks (toilet, shower, wash basin)
  • • Solar panel mounting points with optional battery storage integration
  • • LED lighting fixtures and USB charging points as standard

Flexible Interior Layout Design

  • • Partition systems for family privacy
  • • Slip-resistant flooring for elderly and mobility-impaired residents
  • • Accessible ramp entrances and wider door frames for wheelchair users

Foundation Flexibility

Modular refugee container shelters can be erected on compacted gravel, concrete blocks, steel foundations, wooden beams, or temporary foundations, which is crucial in areas where traditional foundations are unsuitable, such as earthquake-prone regions or flood-prone areas.

Pricing varies based on configuration, insulation specification, installed systems, and shipping destination. Request a tailored quote with our contact form.

Real-World Use Cases and Applications

The applications of rapid deploy refugee container shelters extend far beyond post-earthquake reconstruction. Here's how organizations are deploying:

  • Refugee Camps and Displaced Persons: According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the average duration of exile for refugees is approximately 20 years. Prefab housing for displaced persons can offer a more sustainable solution for the homeless.
  • Emergency Housing: Container disaster relief housing is most commonly used in the aftermath of earthquakes, typhoons, floods, and wildfires, where its rapid deployment provides temporary emergency shelter.
  • Mobile Medical Facilities: Modular housing units can be configured as field hospitals, isolation wards, medical centers, or vaccination stations based on on-site needs.
  • Command and Operations Centers: Provide secure, weatherproof mobile command centers, communication hubs, and coordination facilities for disaster response.
  • Storage and Infrastructure: In emergencies, weatherproof outdoor storage units are essential for protecting critical supplies—such as food, drinking water, and medicine—from environmental degradation, moisture, and contamination.
  • Sanitation Facilities: Equipped with portable toilets, showers, and sanitation stations, designed to address public health issues faced by disaster-displaced populations.

Common Challenges and How to Address Them

Thermal Comfort in Extreme Climates

Steel structures conduct heat and cold efficiently — a feature that works against comfort without proper insulation. We address this with climate-specific insulation packages: EPS for standard applications, rock wool for fire resistance, and high-R-value PU foam for arctic or extreme tropical environments.

Corrosion and Longevity

Standard container homes corrode rapidly when used in humid, coastal, or chemically aggressive environments. All types of our refugee housing units use galvanized steel frames with anti-corrosion protective coatings that resist further corrosion.

Regulatory Compliance and International Acceptance

NEW BRAND manufactures under an ISO 9001-certified quality management system, and carries CE certification. This certification profile satisfies the procurement requirements of UN agencies, ICRC, and national emergency management frameworks.

Unpredictable Road Conditions

The flat-pack and foldable homes are specifically designed for scenarios where crane access is unavailable — panels are sized and weighted for manual handling and assembly with basic hand tools.

Why NEW BRAND Is a Trusted Refugee Housing Unit Supplier?

Since its founding in [Year], NEW BRAND has served customers in more than 60 countries and has built one of the industry's most comprehensive portfolios of prefab buildings and modular homes. Here are key strengths:

  • • Mature Production: ISO 9001-certified manufacturing processes; products comply with CE standards and meet the procurement frameworks of the United Nations and non-governmental organizations.
  • • Comprehensive Product Range: Expandable, foldable, detachable, flat-pack, portable toilets, and mobile medical configurations to cover all scenarios.
  • • 24/7 Support: Our sales and logistics teams operate around the clock to support time-sensitive disaster response procurement.
  • • End-to-End Services: In addition to manufacturing, we can assist with site planning, logistics coordination, assembly training, and post-deployment after-sales support.
  • • Full Customization: Each refugee housing unit can be customized to meet client requirements, including living spaces, utility configurations, accessibility standards, and branding.

Whether you're planning for advance procurement, responding to crises, or building a national emergency housing reserve, our team can help you find the ideal solution that meets your specifications and disaster response timelines. Contact us immediately and provide your location, population size, schedule, budget, and any specific compliance requirements so we can provide you with a quote and design proposal for refugee container shelters.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Fast Can a Refugee Housing Unit be Deployed On-site?

The foldable and flat-pack units can be transported and made operational within 24 to 48 hours of arrival on site under normal ground conditions. Modular medical or multi-room configurations may require 2 to 5 days, depending on the scope of the build and local site preparation.

Do Refugee Rescue Shelters Require a Concrete Foundation?

No permanent foundation is required. NEW BRAND refugee shelters can be placed on compacted gravel or soil (with basic ground leveling), concrete blocks, steel base frames, or temporary concrete slabs — giving field teams maximum flexibility when working in disaster-affected terrain.

Can Refugee Container Shelters be Used for Medical or Healthcare Purposes?

Yes. NEW BRAND offers mobile medical containers that can be configured as field hospitals, wards, operating rooms, temporary clinics, vaccination stations, and diagnostic laboratories. These container units are built from Corten steel and can be equipped with solar power and independent water purification systems for complete off-grid healthcare delivery.

How Long Do Modular Refugee Containers Last, and Can They Be Reused?

NEW BRAND refugee container camps are rated for a service life exceeding 20 years. Their galvanized steel frames are engineered to withstand repeated assembly, disassembly, and redeployment across multiple projects — making them a far more cost-effective long-term investment compared to single-use refugee tents.

Are Container Refugee Camps Customizable for Specific Climates or Populations?

Absolutely. NEW BRAND offers climate-specific insulation materials, slip-resistant flooring, solar panel integration, partition layouts, sanitation facilities, and accessibility modifications designed for vulnerable populations, including the elderly and individuals with disabilities.

How Many Units Can Fit in a Standard Shipping Container for Transport?

The detachable container house units achieve logistics efficiency: approximately 7–8 units can be shipped in a single 20GP container, and 17–18 units in a 40HQ container — dramatically reducing per-unit freight costs compared to pre-assembled shipping methods.

How Do I Request a Quote or Get in Touch with NEW BRAND?

You can reach NEW BRAND's 24/7 procurement team by email at NEW BRAND@NEW BRAND.com or via WhatsApp at [New company phone]. We will then develop a preliminary proposal that includes unit layouts, logistics plans, and reference pricing.
